title: Checks nullable string-based fields (like CharField and TextField) in Django models.
summary: If a string-based field is nullable, then your model will have two possible representations for "no data": None and the empty string. This can lead to confusion, as clients of the API have to check for both None and the empty string when trying to determine if the field has data. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-django and made it stable in v0.0.246.
message_templates: Avoid using `null=True` on string-based fields such as `{}`

title: Checks for the use of locals() in render functions.
summary: Using locals() can expose internal variables or other unintentional data to the rendered template. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-django and made it stable in v0.0.253.
message_templates: Avoid passing `locals()` as context to a `render` function

title: Checks for the use of exclude in Django ModelForm classes.
summary: If a ModelForm includes the exclude attribute, any new field that is added to the model will automatically be exposed for modification. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-django and made it stable in v0.0.253.
message_templates: Do not use `exclude` with `ModelForm`, use `fields` instead

title: Checks for the use of fields = "__all__" in Django ModelForm classes.
summary: If a ModelForm includes the fields = "__all__" attribute, any new field that is added to the model will automatically be exposed for modification. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-django and made it stable in v0.0.253.
message_templates: Do not use `__all__` with `ModelForm`, use `fields` instead

title: Checks that a __str__ method is defined in Django models.
summary: Django models should define a __str__ method to return a string representation of the model instance, as Django calls this method to display the object in the Django Admin and elsewhere. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-django and made it stable in v0.0.246.

title: Checks for the order of Model's inner classes, methods, and fields as per the Django Style Guide.
summary: The Django Style Guide specifies that the order of Model inner classes, attributes and methods should be as follows: Ruff takes this rule from flake8-django and made it stable in v0.0.258.
message_templates: Order of model's inner classes, methods, and fields does not follow the Django Style Guide: {} should come before {}

title: Checks that Django's @receiver decorator is listed first, prior to any other decorators.
summary: Django's @receiver decorator is special in that it does not return a wrapped function. Rather, @receiver connects the decorated function to a signal. If any other decorators are listed before @receiver, the decorated function will not be connected to the signal. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-django and made it stable in v0.0.246.
message_templates: `@receiver` decorator must be on top of all the other decorators
